purpose: Daily affirmations for the Yoga Mom Talk and OhioMom front pages: a kind word for moms going through a hard time, in Deborah's speech bubble, each with the picture that goes with it. The card shows one a day, by the visitor's date, and a visitor can flip to others. Only affirmations with approved true are published. cast lists the children who are around in the picture (an empty list is Deborah alone); pose and sweater are optional too. Whatever an affirmation leaves out takes its turn. do says what a child is doing (otherwise each child's activities take turns). when is thanksgiving, winter or night: such an affirmation is in the turn only in its season, or only after bedtime, by the visitor's clock.

affirmations.text: You do not have to do it all today. The next small thing is enough.
Tired is not the same as failing. You are tired because you keep showing up.
The dishes can wait. You are allowed to sit down for five minutes.
Cereal for dinner still counts as feeding your family.
Rest is not something you have to earn. You are allowed to rest right now.
Some days the win is that everyone made it to bedtime. That is a real win.
You are doing more than anyone sees. I see it.
A messy house and loved kids. That is a good trade.
Your best looks different on a hard day, and it still counts.
One deep breath. Drop your shoulders. You are doing okay.
It is okay to lower the bar today. You can raise it again another day.
Asking for help is a strong thing to do, not a weak one.
You are allowed to say no to one more thing.
If today felt lonely, you are not the only mom who felt that way. There are a lot of us.
You deserve a friend who asks how you are and waits for the answer.
It is okay to reach out first. Most moms are hoping someone will.
Feeling unseen does not mean you do not matter. You matter a great deal.
Your feelings make sense. You are not too much.
You do not have to explain your hard day here. We get it.
A text to another mom that says “me too” can turn a whole day around.
Feeding, changing, rocking, repeat. That is real work, even when it looks like sitting still.
You and your baby are still learning each other. There is no rush.
The days with a newborn are long. This stretch will not last forever.
If all you did today was keep a tiny person fed and warm, you did a big job.
You do not need to bounce back. You can just be where you are.
However your baby is fed, you are taking care of your baby. That is what counts.
You can be short on sleep and full of love at the same time.
Hold the baby and let the house go. The house will still be here.
A meltdown in the store does not make you a bad mom. It means you have a toddler.
Little ones test the limits because they feel safe with you.
You stayed calm one minute longer than yesterday. That counts.
If you lost your temper, a hug and a sorry fixes a lot. That teaches them something good too.
Sticky hands, loud voices, big feelings. You are raising a whole person.
The fifth “why?” of the hour is a little mind growing.
You do not need a perfect day to make a happy memory.
A slammed door is not the end of the story. Keep the porch light on.
Your teen may not say it, but your steady presence matters.
Being the calm one in the house is hard work. You are doing it.
Some of the best talks happen in the car. Keep driving.
They pull away to grow up, not to leave you behind.
You do not need every answer. Listening is a big part of it.
Big kids still need you, just in quieter ways.
Doing it on your own takes a strength most people never see.
You are enough parent for your child. You always have been.
One set of hands, a hundred jobs. Go easy on yourself.
Your kids are learning what a strong, loving person looks like by watching you.
Taking a break is not leaving your post. It is how you keep going.
Nobody is keeping score. Love and showing up are what matter.
Grief and love come from the same place. Missing someone shows how much you loved them.
There is no right timeline for grief. Take the time you need.
On the hard anniversaries, be as gentle with yourself as you would be with a friend.
You can carry sadness and still laugh with your kids. Both are real.
If you lost a pregnancy or a baby, that loss is real, and so is your love.
Some days grief is quiet and some days it is loud. Both are okay.
Being short on money does not make you short on love.
Your kids will remember the time with you more than the things you bought.
Asking about help with bills is smart, not shameful. That is what the help is there for.
A free afternoon at the park can be the best day of the week.
You stretched it one more week. That takes real skill.
Worrying about money is tiring. You are carrying a lot, and you are still here.
You drank a glass of water today. Start there.
Everyone got out the door. The shoes may not have matched. Still a win.
You made the phone call you were dreading. That was brave.
You laughed today. Hold on to that.
A warm meal, a clean shirt, a bedtime story. Small things add up to a childhood.
Today you were kind to someone, even if it was only yourself.
Progress, not perfect. You moved forward today.
You finished one thing on the list. That is one more than none.
You are a good mom. The fact that you worry about it shows how much you care.
You are more than what you get done in a day.
Your kids do not need a perfect mom. They need you, and they have you.
Be as patient with yourself as you are with your kids.
You are allowed to take up space, to want things and to have your own dreams.
A mistake does not cancel out love. Tomorrow is a fresh start.
You are someone’s whole world, and you are also your own person.
It is okay not to love every minute. You can still love your kids with your whole heart.
There is no one right way to be a mom. Your way is allowed.
Like tree pose, it is okay to wobble. You can find your balance again.
Plant your feet like mountain pose. You are steadier than you feel.
Warrior two: strong legs, open arms. That is you, facing this week.
Breathe in for four, out for four. You are right here, and you are doing okay.
Stretch wide like a star. You are allowed to take up room.
A wide, low squat is hard to hold. So is a long day. You are holding it.
You can lean like a crescent moon and still be standing.
You do not have to reach your toes yet. Every bit of a stretch counts.
Triangle pose: one hand down, one hand up. Stay grounded and keep reaching.
It is late. Whatever did not get done today can wait until tomorrow.
Up with the baby at this hour? Lots of moms are awake with you right now.
The house is quiet. This moment is yours. Breathe.
You made it through today. That is all today needed.
If your mind is busy tonight, write it down and let it wait until morning.
Rest your eyes. Tomorrow you get to start again.
Holidays can be hard as well as happy. Whatever this season feels like for you is okay.
The table does not need to be perfect. The people around it are what matter.
If you are missing someone at the table this year, be gentle with your heart.
Thank you, mom, for every meal, every ride and every hug.
You do not have to host, bake or smile through all of it. A simple holiday is still a holiday.
The best gift your kids get this year is time with you.
A small holiday is still full of love. It does not take a lot of money to make it special.
Cold days, warm hugs. You are the warm place in your house.
It is okay to skip some of the holiday rush. Peace counts as a present.
If the season is heavy this year, you are not alone. Take it one day at a time.
